title: Talaffuz klinikasi
goal_uz: Dars oxirida o‘zbek tilida yo‘q ovozlarni — /θ/, /ð/, /w/, /æ/, qisqa va uzun unlilar, schwa — to‘g‘ri talaffuz qilasiz; so‘z urg‘usini va jumla ritmini bilasiz; savol va sanash ohanglarini ajratasiz; kamida yigirma ta minimal juftlikni to‘g‘ri o‘qiy olasiz.

vocab.uz: minimal juftlik (faqat bitta ovoz bilan farq qiluvchi so‘zlar)
schwa — ingliz tilidagi eng ko‘p uchraydigan noaniq ovoz (/ə/)
zaif shakl (a, the, to, of kabi so‘zlarning qisqa talaffuzi)
ritm (urg‘uli va zaif bo‘g‘inlarning navbatma-navbat kelishi)

scenes.title: Bugun: talaffuz klinikasi
board: Missing sounds · Stress · Rhythm · Intonation · Minimal pairs
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda so‘zlashuv iboralarini o‘rgangan edik. Bugun talaffuz klinikasiga tashrif buyuramiz: o‘zbek tilida yo‘q ovozlarni tuzatamiz — th, w, æ, qisqa va uzun unlilar. So‘z urg‘usi, jumla ritmi va savol hamda sanashning ohangini ham o‘rganamiz. Dars oxirida yigirma ta minimal juftlikni to‘g‘ri o‘qiy olasiz. Boshlaymiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back! Last time we covered conversational phrases. Today we go to the pronunciation clinic. We'll fix the sounds Uzbek doesn't have — th, w, the short “a”, short and long vowels. We'll also cover word stress, sentence rhythm and question and list intonation. By the end, you'll read twenty minimal pairs correctly. Let's begin.
scenes.say_uz: Qaytganingiz bilan! O‘tgan darsda so‘zlashuv iboralarini ko‘rib chiqqandik. Bugun talaffuz klinikasi: o‘zbek tilida yo‘q ovozlarni tuzatamiz — th, w, qisqa “a”, qisqa va uzun unlilar. So‘z urg‘usi, jumla ritmi va savol hamda sanash ohangini ham o‘rganamiz. Dars oxirida yigirma ta minimal juftlikni to‘g‘ri o‘qiy olasiz. Boshlaymiz.

scenes.title: Nega talaffuz muhim?
board: Grammar can be perfect and still unclear
One sound can change the whole word
scenes.say_native: Nega talaffuz shunchalik muhim? Grammatikangiz mukammal bo‘lsa ham, bir ovoz noto‘g‘ri bo‘lsa so‘z ma’nosi butunlay o‘zgaradi. Bitta misol: “I sink this number” — bu “Men bu sonni cho‘kaman” emas, balki “I think this number” — “Menimcha, bu son” degani. Britaniya ingliz tilini IELTS’da, intervyularda va ish uchrashuvlarida toza talaffuz bo‘lsa tinglovchilar sizni oson tushunadi.
scenes.say: Why does pronunciation matter so much? Your grammar can be perfect and still be misunderstood — one sound can change the meaning of the whole word. “I sink this” versus “I think this.” Clean pronunciation makes interviews, meetings and the IELTS listening and speaking tests far easier.
scenes.say_uz: Nega talaffuz shunchalik muhim? Grammatikangiz mukammal bo‘lsa ham, bitta ovoz noto‘g‘ri bo‘lsa so‘z ma’nosi butunlay o‘zgaradi. “I sink this” — “Men bu sonni cho‘kaman”, “I think this” — “Menimcha, bu son”. Toza talaffuz intervyularda va IELTS nutqi bo‘limida sizni oson tushunishini ta’minlaydi.

scenes.title: Ovozlar /θ/ va /ð/: ikki qoidasi
board: /θ/ (soft): think, three, thank — tongue between teeth
/ð/ (buzz): this, that, mother — tongue between teeth + voice

examples.t: Put your tongue between your teeth.

scenes.say_native: Th tovushining ikki turi bor. Birinchi — /θ/ — pishillaydigan: think, three, thank. Tilingizni tishlaringiz orasiga qo‘ying va pishillating — sovuq shamol. Ikkinchi — /ð/ — qo‘ng‘iroqchalidek: this, that, mother, weather. Xuddi shunday til holati, lekin tovush titrashi bor. O‘zbek tilida bu ovozlar yo‘q, shuning uchun o‘rganuvchilar “sank”, “dis” deyishadi. Endi mashq qilamiz.
scenes.say: The “th” has two types. First, voiceless — “think, three, thank”: put your tongue between your teeth and blow — like a cold wind. Second, voiced — “this, that, mother, weather”: same tongue position, but with your voice buzzing. Uzbek has neither sound, so learners often say “sink” or “dis.” Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Th tovushining ikki turi bor. Birinchi — /θ/ — pishillaydigan: think, three, thank — tilni tishlar orasiga qo‘ying va pishillating, sovuq shamoldek. Ikkinchi — /ð/ — titragichi bor: this, that, mother, weather — til bir xil, lekin tovush titraydi. O‘zbek tilida bu ovozlar yo‘q, shuning uchun ko‘pchilik “sank” yoki “dis” deydi. Endi mashq qilamiz.

scenes.title: /θ/ mashqi
board: think · three · thank · thin · teeth · thick
Read each aloud, tongue between teeth
scenes.say_native: Mashq. /θ/ tovushini o‘qib chiqing: think, three, thank, thin, teeth, thick. Tilni tishlar orasiga qo‘yib pishillating. Har birini uch marta takrorlang. E’tibor bering: sira “s” chiqarmaslik kerak.
scenes.say: Read aloud with your tongue between your teeth: think, three, thank, thin, teeth, thick. Repeat each three times — no “ssss” sound at all.
scenes.say_uz: Tilni tishlar orasiga qo‘yib baland ovozda o‘qing: think, three, thank, thin, teeth, thick. Har birini uch marta takrorlang — “sss” ovozi chiqmasin.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: think — o‘ylamoq, three — uch, thank — rahmat aytmoq. Endi /ð/ tovushini mashq qilamiz: this, that, these, those, mother, weather. Xuddi shunday til holatida, lekin titroq bilan — sovuq shamol emas, ari ovozi.
scenes.say: Answers: think, three, thank. Now the voiced one: this, that, these, those, mother, weather. Same tongue position, but voiced — not a cold wind, more like a bee.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: think, three, thank. Endi titragichi bor: this, that, these, those, mother, weather. Til holati bir xil, lekin titraq bilan — sovuq shamol emas, asalarining ovozi.

scenes.title: /ð/ mashqi va th juftliklar
board: bath vs bathe · thigh vs thy
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Birinchi: this, that, these, those, mother, weather — titroq bilan. Ikkinchi: bath — vannaxona (pishillaydi) vs bathe — cho‘milmoq (titraydi). Thigh — son vs thy — “sening” degan eski so‘z. Tilingizni tishlar orasiga qo‘yib o‘qing.
scenes.say: First read this, that, these, those, mother, weather with a buzz. Then the pairs: bath keeps the soft sound, bathe has the buzz; thigh is soft, thy is voiced. Tongue between your teeth both times.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchi: this, that, these, those, mother, weather — titroq bilan. Keyin juftliklar: bath — yumshoq, bathe — titroq; thigh — yumshoq, thy — titraq. Tilni ikkala holatda ham tishlar orasiga qo‘ying.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: bath — “bæth”, yumshoq; bathe — “baydh”, titroq. Thigh — “thay”, yumshoq; thy — shu yozuvchi, titraq. Endi ingliz tilida yo‘q ovozlari haqidagi eng mashhur xatoni ko‘ramiz.
scenes.say: Answers: bath ends soft, bathe ends buzzed; thigh is soft, thy is buzzed. Same spelling family, one sound changes everything. Now the most famous th mistake.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: bath — yumshoq yakun, bathe — titroq yakun; thigh — yumshoq, thy — titraq. Bir xil yozuvcha, bitta ovoz hammasini o‘zgartiradi. Endi eng mashhur th xatosi.

scenes.title: Keng tarqalgan xato: “tree” va “three”
scenes.say_native: Keng tarqalgan xato: “tree” va “three”ni adashtirish. “I have tree sons” ingliz tilida kulgili yangraydi — “Menim uchta daraxtim bor”. “I’m free” — “Men bo‘shman”, “I’m three” — “Men uch yoshdaman”. Ovoz farqi: three — til tishlar orasida, free — tishlar bir-biriga tegib, ovoz “f” bilan boshlanadi. Endi bu juftliklarni mashq qilamiz.
scenes.say: The classic mistake: mixing up “tree” and “three.” “I have tree sons” sounds comical to an English ear. “I'm free” means you have time; “I'm three” means you are three years old. The difference: in “three” your tongue is between your teeth; in “free” your teeth and lip make an “f.” Now the drill.
scenes.say_uz: Eng keng tarqalgan xato: “tree” va “three”ni adashtirish. “I have tree sons” ingliz qulog‘iga kulgili eshitiladi. “I'm free” — “Menim vaqtim boy”, “I'm three” — “Men uchdayman”. Farq: “three”da til tishlar orasida; “free”da tish va lab “f” hosil qiladi. Endi mashqqa.

scenes.title: three — free juftlik mashqi
board: three / free · think / fink · thigh / fye
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Juftliklarni navbat bilan o‘qing: three — free, think — fink, thigh — fye. Endi gapni ovoz chiqarib o‘qing: “There are three free parking spaces.” — tilni ikkala joyga qo‘yib o‘qing.
scenes.say: Read the pairs in turn: three — free, think — fink, thigh — fye. Then the sentence aloud: “There are three free parking spaces.” Careful with the “th” every single time.
scenes.say_uz: Juftliklarni navbat bilan o‘qing: three — free, think — fink, thigh — fye. Endi gapni baland ovozda o‘qing: “There are three free parking spaces.” Har safar “th”ni to‘g‘ri ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: three — til tishlar orasida, free — lab va tish. Gapni o‘qiganingizda “th” har doim aniq bo‘lsin. Endi w va v tovushlariga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: three — tongue between the teeth; free — lip and teeth. Keep the “th” crisp every time. Now the w and v sounds.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: three — til tishlar orasida; free — lab va tish. Har safar “th”ni tiniq tut. Endi w va v.

scenes.title: W va V tovushlari
board: /v/ — top teeth + lower lip: vet, vine, vest
scenes.say_native: W va v: ingliz tilidagi /w/ ovozi lablarni dumaloq qilib, “u”ga o‘xshab boshlanadi: wet, wine, west. /v/ ovozi yuqori tishlar va pastki lab orasida: vet, vine, vest. O‘zbek tilida /w/ yo‘q, faqat /v/ bor — shuning uchun “vinegar” ni “wvinegar” deb yoki aksincha “wine” ni “vine” deb aytasiz. Endi mashq qilamiz.
scenes.say: The sounds w and v. English /w/ starts with rounded lips, like a “u” — wet, wine, west. English /v/ uses your top teeth on your lower lip — vet, vine, vest. Uzbek has /v/ but not /w/, so learners often swap them — “vine” for “wine.” Now the drill.
scenes.say_uz: W va v: inglizcha /w/ — lablar dumaloq, “u”ga o‘xshab boshlanadi: wet, wine, west. /v/ — yuqori tish va pastki lab orasida: vet, vine, vest. O‘zbek tilida /w/ yo‘q, faqat /v/ bor — shuning uchun “wine”ni “vine” deb aytadilar. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: W — V juftlik mashqi
board: wet / vet · wine / vine · west / vest · worse / verse
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Juftliklarni o‘qing: wet — vet, wine — vine, west — vest, worse — verse. Lablaringizni dumaloq qiling w da, tish va lab v da. Keyin gapni o‘qing: “This wine is very fine.” — ichida ham w, ham v bor.
scenes.say: Read the pairs: wet — vet, wine — vine, west — vest, worse — verse. Round your lips for w; teeth-on-lip for v. Then the sentence: “This wine is very fine.” — it has both.
scenes.say_uz: Juftliklarni o‘qing: wet — vet, wine — vine, west — vest, worse — verse. W da lablarni dumaloq qiling, v da tish va lab. Keyin gap: “This wine is very fine.” — ichida ham w, ham v bor.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: “wine not vine” — har safar lablar dumaloq
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: wet — “u”ga o‘xshab boshlanadigan w; vet — tish va lab v. “Wine” ni to‘g‘ri aytsangiz, ingliz qulog‘i sizni darrov tushunadi. Endi qisqa unlilarga o‘tamiz — /æ/ va /ʌ/.
scenes.say: Answers: wet starts round like “u,” vet is teeth and lip. Say “wine” properly and English listeners understand you immediately. Now short vowels — the short “a” and the “u” in “cup.”
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: wet — “u”ga o‘xshab boshlanadi, vet — tish va lab. “Wine”ni to‘g‘ri aytsangiz, ingliz tinglovchisi sizni darrov tushunadi. Endi qisqa unlilar — “a” va “u”.

scenes.title: /æ/ va /ʌ/: cat va cut
board: /æ/ — cat, man, bad — mouth wide, short
/ʌ/ — cut, sun, bud — mouth less open, central
bad / bed / bud — three different vowels

examples.t: The cat sat on the mat.

scenes.say_native: Qisqa unlilar: /æ/ — cat, man, bad — og‘zingiz keng ochiladi, iyakingiz pastga tushadi, ovoz qisqa va keskin. /ʌ/ — cup, cut, sun — og‘zingiz kamroq ochiladi, markazga yaqin, ovoz qisqa va chuqur. O‘zbek tilidagi “a” bundan oraliqda, shuning uchun ikkalasini ham bir xil aytasiz. Endi uchta unlini solishtiramiz.
scenes.say: Two short vowels. The short “a” — cat, man, bad — mouth wide open, jaw drops, short and sharp. The “uh” in cup — cup, cut, sun — mouth less open, more central, short and deep. Uzbek “a” sits between the two, so learners flatten both. Let's compare three.
scenes.say_uz: Ikki qisqa unli: qisqa “a” — cat, man, bad — og‘iz keng ochiladi, iyak tushadi, qisqa va keskin. “u” cup, cut, sun — og‘iz kamroq ochiladi, qisqa va chuqur. O‘zbek tilining “a”si ikkalasi orasida, shuning uchun ikkalasini ham bir xil aytasiz. Uchtasini solishtiramiz.

scenes.title: cat — cut — bet mashqi
board: hear the set: cat cut bet bad bud bed
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uchta ovozni navbat bilan o‘qing: cat, bet, cut — cat, cut, bet. Endi to‘liq to‘plam: cat, bet, cut, bad, bed, bud. Og‘zingizning shakli har o‘qishda o‘zgarishini sezing. Har birini uch marta takrorlang.
scenes.say: Read the three sounds in turn: cat, bet, cut — cat, cut, bet. Then the full set: cat, bet, cut, bad, bed, bud. Feel your mouth change shape every time. Repeat each three times.
scenes.say_uz: Uch ovozni navbat bilan o‘qing: cat, bet, cut — cat, cut, bet. Keyin to‘liq to‘plam: cat, bet, cut, bad, bed, bud. Og‘zingizning shakli har safar o‘zgarishini his qiling. Har birini uch marta takrorlang.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: cat — keng /æ/, bet — o‘rta /e/, cut — markaziy /ʌ/. Endi eng muhim farqni ko‘ramiz: qisqa “i” va uzun “ii” — ship va sheep.
scenes.say: Answers: cat — wide short “a,” bet — mid “e,” cut — central “uh.” Now the most important contrast in English: short “i” versus long “ee.”
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: cat — keng qisqa “a”, bet — o‘rta “e”, cut — markaziy “u”. Endi ingliz tilidagi eng muhim farq: qisqa “i” va uzun “ii”.

scenes.title: Ship va sheep: qisqa va uzun i
board: live / leave · fit / feet · sit / seat
scenes.say_native: Eng muhim farq: qisqa “i” — ship, /ɪ/ — og‘iz bo‘shashgan, mushaklar tarang emas, qisqa. Uzun “ii” — sheep, /iː/ — og‘iz cho‘zilgan, mushaklar tarang, tabassum bilan, cho‘ziq. “Live” — yashamoq, “leave” — ketmoq. “Fit” — mos kelmoq, “feet” — oyoqlar. O‘zbek tilida ikkalasiga bitta “i” yetadi, shuning uchun “ship” va “sheep” bir xil eshitiladi. Endi mashq qilamiz.
scenes.say: The most important contrast. Short “i” — ship — mouth relaxed, lips loose, very short. Long “ee” — sheep — mouth stretched into a smile, muscles tense, held longer. “Live” means to reside; “leave” means to go. “Fit” is to be the right size; “feet” are what you walk on. Uzbek uses one “i” for both, so learners merge them. Now the drill.
scenes.say_uz: Eng muhim farq: qisqa “i” — ship — og‘iz bo‘shashgan, lablar bo‘sh, juda qisqa. Uzun “ii” — sheep — og‘iz tabassumga cho‘zilgan, mushaklar tarang, cho‘ziq. “Live” — yashamoq, “leave” — ketmoq. “Fit” — mos kelmoq, “feet” — oyoqlar. O‘zbek tilida ikkalasiga bitta “i” yetadi — shuning uchun “ship” va “sheep” bir xil eshitiladi. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: ship — sheep mashqi
board: ship / sheep · live / leave · fit / feet
sit / seat · his / he's · miss / niece? use: miss / lease
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Juftliklarni o‘qing: ship — sheep, live — leave, fit — feet, sit — seat. Endi murakkab gapni o‘qing: “The sheep on the ship were fit for feet.” Tabassum bilan uzun “ii”ni cho‘zib o‘qing.
scenes.say: Read the pairs: ship — sheep, live — leave, fit — feet, sit — seat. Then the tricky sentence: “The sheep on the ship were fit for feet.” Hold the long “ee” with a smile.
scenes.say_uz: Juftliklarni o‘qing: ship — sheep, live — leave, fit — feet, sit — seat. Keyin murakkab gap: “The sheep on the ship were fit for feet.” Uzun “ii”ni tabassum bilan cho‘zib o‘qing.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: ship — qisqa, sheep — uzun; live — yashamoq, leave — ketmoq. Tabassum uzun unlini beradi. Endi schwa tovushiga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: ship — short, sheep — long; live — to reside, leave — to go. A smile is what makes the long vowel. Now the schwa.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: ship — qisqa, sheep — uzun; live — yashamoq, leave — ketmoq. Tabassum uzun unlini beradi. Endi schwa.

scenes.title: Schwa: ingliz tilining eng ko‘p uchraydigan ovozi
board: any vowel letter can become schwa

examples.t: a cup of tea — “uh cup uh tea”
examples.uz: a cup of tea — “uh cup uh tea”

scenes.say_native: Schwa — ingliz tilining eng ko‘p uchraydigan ovozi: /ə/ — “guh”ga o‘xshash noaniq ovoz. “The”, “a”, “of”, “to”, “about”, “sofa”, “today”, “China” — barchasida bor. Qoida: zaif bo‘g‘indagi unli harf schwa bo‘ladi. O‘zbek tilida ham zaif bo‘g‘inlar borku, lekin ingliz tilida bu alohida ovoz sifatida o‘rganilishi shart. Endi mashq qilamiz.
scenes.say: The schwa is the most common sound in English — a lazy “uh,” like in “the,” “a,” “about,” “sofa,” “today,” “China.” The rule: any vowel letter in a weak syllable can become schwa. Uzbek has weak syllables too, but English treats this as a distinct sound. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Schwa — ingliz tilining eng ko‘p uchraydigan ovozi: dangasa “uh”ga o‘xshash noaniq tovush — “the”, “a”, “about”, “sofa”, “today”, “China”da bor. Qoida: zaif bo‘g‘indagi har qanday unli schwa bo‘lishi mumkin. O‘zbek tilida ham zaif bo‘g‘inlar bor, lekin ingliz tilida bu alohida ovoz. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Schwa mashqi
board: a cup of tea · the best of both · today and tomorrow
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ikkita to‘plamni o‘qing: birinchi — “a cup of tea”, “the best of both”, “today and tomorrow” — zaif so‘zlar dangasa. Ikkinchi — about, above, again, banana — birinchi va oxirgi bo‘g‘inlar schwa. Har birini uch marta takrorlang.
scenes.say: Read two sets. First: “a cup of tea,” “the best of both,” “today and tomorrow” — lazy weak words. Second: about, above, again, banana — first and last syllables are schwa. Repeat each three times.
scenes.say_uz: Ikki to‘plamni o‘qing. Birinchi: “a cup of tea”, “the best of both”, “today and tomorrow” — zaif so‘zlar dangasa. Ikkinchi: about, above, again, banana — birinchi va oxirgi bo‘g‘inlar schwa. Har birini uch marta takrorlang.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: a cup of tea — zaif: uh cup uh tea
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: a cup of tea — “uh cup uh tea”; about, again — birinchi bo‘g‘in schwa. Endi so‘z urg‘usiga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: “a cup of tea” is “uh cup uh tea”; about and again start with schwa. Now word stress.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “a cup of tea” — “uh cup uh tea”; about va again — schwa bilan boshlanadi. Endi so‘z urg‘usi.

scenes.title: So‘z urg‘usi
board: PHOtograph vs phoTOgraphy — different parts of the word carry the beat
-tion words stress the syllable before: na-TION
-ity words stress the syllable before: nationALity, possibility

examples.t: A PHOtograph of the phoTOgraphy club.

scenes.say_native: So‘z urg‘usi: ingliz tilida har bir uzun so‘zda bitta urg‘uli bo‘g‘in bor. “PHOtograph” — birinchi bo‘g‘in; “phoTOgraphy” — ikkinchi bo‘g‘in; “photoGRAPHic” — uchinchi. Qoidalar: “-tion”li so‘zlarda urg‘u -tiondan oldingi bo‘g‘inda: naTION, creATION. “-ity”li so‘zlarda ham urg‘u qo‘shimchadan oldingi bo‘g‘inda: nationALIty, possibILity. Asosiy g‘oya: so‘z kengayganda urg‘u harakatlanadi — shuning uchun har doim bo‘g‘inlarni sanang. Endi mashq qilamiz.
scenes.say: Word stress: every long English word has one stressed syllable. “PHOtograph” stresses the first; “phoTOgraphy,” the second; “photoGRAPHic,” the third. For “-tion” words, stress the syllable before “-tion” — naTION, creATION. For “-ity,” stress the syllable before it as well — nationALIty. The key idea: the beat can move as the word changes. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: So‘z urg‘usi: har bir uzun ingliz so‘zida bitta urg‘uli bo‘g‘in bor. “PHOtograph” — birinchi bo‘g‘in; “phoTOgraphy” — ikkinchi; “photoGRAPHic” — uchinchi. “-tion”li so‘zlarda urg‘u -tiondan oldin: naTION, creATION; “-ity”lilarida ham -itydan oldin. Asosiy g‘oya: so‘z kengayganda urg‘u harakatlanadi. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Urg‘uni toping
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uchta juftlikni urg‘u bilan o‘qing: “OBject” — “narsa” degani ot, “obJECT” — “e’tiroz bildirmoq” degani fe’l. “REcord” — “rekord/yozuv” degani ot, “reCORD” — “yozib olmoq” degani fe’l. PROtest — ot, proTEST — fe’l. Har birini ikki marta takrorlang.
scenes.say: Read three pairs with stress. “OBject” — noun, a thing; “obJECT” — verb, to disagree. “REcord” — noun, an entry; “reCORD” — verb, to capture. “PROtest” — noun; “proTEST” — verb. Repeat each twice.
scenes.say_uz: Uchta juftlikni urg‘u bilan o‘qing. “OBject” — ot, narsa; “obJECT” — fe’l, e’tiroz bildirmoq. “REcord” — ot, yozuv; “reCORD” — fe’l, yozib olmoq. “PROtest” — ot; “proTEST” — fe’l. Har birini ikki marta takrorlang.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: OBject — ot, obJECT — fe’l; REcord — ot, reCORD — fe’l; PROtest — ot, proTEST — fe’l. Urg‘u otdan fe’lga ko‘chganda ma’no o‘zgaradi. Endi jumla ritmiga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: OBject — noun, obJECT — verb; REcord — noun, reCORD — verb; PROtest — noun, proTEST — verb. The meaning changes as the beat moves. Now sentence rhythm.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: OBject — ot; obJECT — fe’l; REcord — ot; reCORD — fe’l; PROtest — ot; proTEST — fe’l. Urg‘u ko‘chganda ma’no o‘zgaradi. Endi jumla ritmi.

scenes.title: Jumla ritmi: urg‘uli va zaif so‘zlar
board: Content words stressed: nouns, verbs, adjectives, numbers
Function words weak: a, the, of, to, and

examples.t: I'd LIKE a CUP of TEA.

scenes.say_native: Jumla ritmi: ingliz tilida mazmun so‘zlari — otlar, fe’llar, sifatlar, raqamlar — urg‘ulanadi: “I’d LIKE a CUP of TEA.” Xizmat so‘zlari — a, the, of, to, and — zaif bo‘ladi, deyarli eshitilmaydi. Urg‘ular orasida teng vaqt o‘tadi, zaif bo‘g‘inlar tezroq aytiladi. O‘zbek tilida har bir so‘z bir xil urg‘ulanadi — ingliz tilida esa tekis emas. Endi mashq qilamiz.
scenes.say: Sentence rhythm. In English, the meaning words — nouns, verbs, adjectives, numbers — carry the beat: “I'd LIKE a CUP of TEA.” The function words — a, the, of, to, and — go weak and nearly disappear. The beat stays even; the weak syllables are squeezed in between. Uzbek pushes every syllable equally — English doesn't. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Jumla ritmi: mazmun so‘zlari — otlar, fe’llar, sifatlar, raqamlar — urg‘ulanadi: “I'd LIKE a CUP of TEA.” Xizmat so‘zlari — a, the, of, to, and — zaif bo‘lib, deyarli eshitilmaydi. Urg‘ular orasida teng vaqt — zaif bo‘g‘inlar tezroq aytiladi. O‘zbek tilida har bo‘g‘in bir tekis urg‘ulanadi — ingliz tilida yo‘q. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Ritmni urib chiqing
board: I'd LIKE a CUP of TEA.
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ikki jumlani stulga urib ritmini chizing: “She WENT to the SHOP.” — uch zarb. “I’d LIKE a CUP of TEA.” — uch zarb. Zaif so‘zlar — to, a, of — tez o‘tkazib yuboring. Har birini uch marta takrorlang.
scenes.say: Tap the beat on your desk for two sentences. “She WENT to the SHOP.” — three beats. “I'd LIKE a CUP of TEA.” — three beats. Slip the weak words — to, a, of — through quickly. Repeat each three times.
scenes.say_uz: Ikki jumlaning ritmini stolga urib chizing. “She WENT to the SHOP.” — uch zarb. “I'd LIKE a CUP of TEA.” — uch zarb. Zaif so‘zlarni — to, a, of — tez o‘tkazib yuboring. Har birini uch marta takrorlang.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: I'd LIKE / a CUP / of TEA
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “She WENT to the SHOP” — uch zarb; “I’d LIKE a CUP of TEA” — uch zarb. Endi intonatsiyaga o‘tamiz: savollar va sanash.
scenes.say: Answers: “She WENT to the SHOP” — three beats; “I'd LIKE a CUP of TEA” — three beats. Now intonation — questions and lists.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: “She WENT to the SHOP” — uch zarb; “I'd LIKE a CUP of TEA” — uch zarb. Endi intonatsiya.

scenes.title: Intonatsiya: savollar va sanash
board: Yes/no questions rise: Are you COMING?
Wh-questions fall: WHERE are you going?
Lists rise, rise, fall: apples, bananas, and ORANGES.
scenes.say_native: Intonatsiya: ha-yo‘q savollar so‘ngida ko‘tariladi: “Are you coming?” — “kelyapsizmi?” Wh savollar — nega, qachon, kim — pasayadi: “Where are you going?” — “Qayerga ketyapsiz?” — pasayish bilan. Sanashda esa har element ko‘tariladi, oxirgisida pasayadi: “apples, bananas, and ORANGES.” — “olmalar, bananlar va apelsinlar.” Endi mashq qilamiz.
scenes.say: Intonation. Yes/no questions rise at the end — “Are you coming?” Wh-questions fall — “Where are you going?” Lists rise on each item and fall on the last — “apples, bananas, and ORANGES.” Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Intonatsiya: ha-yo‘q savollar oxirida ko‘tariladi — “Are you coming?” Wh-savollar, ya’ni nega, qachon, kim, pasayadi — “Where are you going?” Sanashda har element ko‘tariladi, oxirgisi pasayadi — “apples, bananas, and ORANGES.” Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Intonatsiya mashqi
board: Are you ready? When are you ready?
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Uch jumlani to‘g‘ri ohang bilan o‘qing: “Are you ready?” — ko‘tarilib. “When are you ready?” — pasayib. “Tea, coffee, and juice” — ko‘tarilib, ko‘tarilib, pasayib. Har birini uch marta takrorlang.
scenes.say: Read three sentences with the right tune: “Are you ready?” rises; “When are you ready?” falls; “tea, coffee, and juice” rises, rises, falls. Repeat each three times.
scenes.say_uz: Uch jumlani to‘g‘ri ohang bilan o‘qing: “Are you ready?” — ko‘tarilib; “When are you ready?” — pasayib; “tea, coffee, and juice” — ko‘tarilib, ko‘tarilib, pasayib. Har birini uch marta takrorlang.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: ha-yo‘q — ko‘tariladi; wh-savol — pasayadi; sanash — oxirida pasayadi. Endi bog‘lash va zaif shakllarni o‘rganamiz — tabiiy nutqning sirlari.
scenes.say: Answers: yes/no — rises; wh-questions — fall; lists — rise then fall at the end. Now linking and weak forms — the secrets of natural speech.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: ha-yo‘q — ko‘tariladi; wh-savol — pasayadi; sanash — oxirida pasayadi. Endi bog‘lash va zaif shakllar — tabiiy nutq sirlari.

scenes.title: Bog‘lash va zaif shakllar
board: want to → wanna · going to → gonna (informal)

examples.t: Pick it up and turn it off.

scenes.say_native: Bog‘lash — bir so‘zning oxiri keyingi so‘zning boshi bilan birga o‘qiladi: “an orange” — “a-norange”, “turn it off” — “tur-ni-toff”. Zaif shakllar: “to”, “of”, “and”, “a”, “the” zaiflashadi. Norasmiy nutqda “want to” “wanna”, “going to” “gonna”ga aylanadi. IELTS og‘zaki nutqida buni tinglash va tushunish muhim. Endi mashq qilamiz.
scenes.say: Linking means the end of one word joins the start of the next: “an orange” flows as “a-norange,” and “turn it off” as “tur-ni-toff.” Weak forms: “to,” “of,” “and,” “a,” and “the” all go lazy. In casual speech “want to” becomes “wanna” and “going to” becomes “gonna.” You need to hear these for the IELTS speaking test. Now practice.
scenes.say_uz: Bog‘lash — bir so‘zning oxiri keyingisining boshi bilan birga o‘qiladi: “an orange” — “a-norange”, “turn it off” — “tur-ni-toff”. Zaif shakllar: to, of, and, a, the dangasa bo‘ladi. Norasmiy nutqda want to — wanna, going to — gonna. IELTS og‘zaki bo‘limida buni eshitib tushunish muhim. Endi mashq.

scenes.title: Bog‘lash mashqi
board: an orange · turn it off · pick it up
want to go · going to leave
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Bog‘lab o‘qing: “an orange”, “turn it off”, “pick it up”. Endi norasmiy: “I wanna go.” “I’m gonna leave.” Rasmiy gapni ham ayting: “I want to go.” Har biri ikki marta.
scenes.say: Link these: “an orange,” “turn it off,” “pick it up.” Then the casual forms: “I wanna go.” “I'm gonna leave.” Then the formal: “I want to go.” Say each twice.
scenes.say_uz: Bog‘lab o‘qing: “an orange”, “turn it off”, “pick it up”. Keyin norasmiy: “I wanna go.” “I'm gonna leave.” Keyin rasmiy: “I want to go.” Har birini ikki marta.

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: bog‘langan holda: a-norange, tur-ni-toff, pick-it-tupp. Wanna va gonna tabiiy nutqda odatiy. Endi yakuniy tinglash mashqiga o‘tamiz.
scenes.say: Answers: linked — a-norange, tur-ni-toff, pick-it-up. “Wanna” and “gonna” are completely normal in casual English. Now the final listening exercise.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: bog‘langan holda — a-norange, tur-ni-toff, pick-it-upp. “Wanna” va “gonna” norasmiy nutqda odatiy. Endi yakuniy tinglash mashqi.

scenes.title: Tinglash: bog‘langan nutq
scenes.say_native: Endi tabiiy nutqni tinglang — kofexona suhbati. Bo‘laklarga bo‘lib eshitganingizdan so‘ng ikkita savolga javob berasiz.
scenes.say: Now listen to natural, linked speech — an order at a café. Two questions follow.
scenes.say_uz: Endi tabiiy, bog‘langan nutqni tinglang — kofexonada buyurtma. Keyin ikkita savol beriladi.

scenes.title: Kofexona matni
board: Hi — can I get a latte to go, please?
Thanks — could I have an orange juice too?
scenes.say_native: Tinglang. Buyurtmadagi bog‘lanishlarga quloq soling: “can I”, “to go”, “an orange”.
scenes.say: Hi — can I get a latte to go, please? Sure — that's four fifty. Thanks — could I have an orange juice too? Of course. That'll be six twenty, then.
scenes.say_uz: Salom — latte olib ketishga olasizmi, iltimos? Albatta — bu to‘rt yarim funt. Rahmat — apelsin sharbatini ham olsam bo‘ladimi? Albatta. U holda olti yigirma bo‘ladi.

scenes.title: Ikki savolga javob bering
board: 1. What did the customer order first?
scenes.say_native: Mashq. Ikki savolga javob bering: mijoz avval nima buyurtma qildi? Keyin nima qo‘shdi? Baland ovozda ingliz tilida javob bering.
scenes.say: Answer two questions aloud: What did the customer order first? What did they add afterwards?
scenes.say_uz: Ikki savolga baland ovozda javob bering: mijoz avval nima buyurtma qildi? Keyin nima qo‘shdi?

scenes.title: Javoblar
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: avval latte olib ketishga, keyin apelsin sharbati. E’tibor bering: “can I” — “kan-ay”, “an orange” — “a-norange” eshitildi. Tabiiy ingliz tilida so‘zlar bir-biriga yopishib ketadi. Endi xatolarni ko‘ramiz.
scenes.say: Answers: first a latte to go, then an orange juice. Notice “can I” came out as “kan-ay” and “an orange” as “a-norange.” Natural English words glue together. Now the common mistakes.
scenes.say_uz: Javoblar: avval latte olib ketishga, keyin apelsin sharbati. E’tibor bering: “can I” — “kan-ay”, “an orange” — “a-norange” bo‘lib eshitildi. Tabiiy ingliz tilida so‘zlar bir-biriga yopishib ketadi. Endi xatolarni ko‘ramiz.

scenes.title: Keng tarqalgan xato: “vivir” yoki “leave” qarshisida “live”
board: ✓ Can you seat the bed? — no: “make the bed”

examples.t: I live in Tashkent, not I leave in Tashkent.

scenes.say_native: Keng tarqalgan xato: “live” va “leave”ni adashtirish. “I leave in Tashkent” ingliz tinglovchisiga tabiiy emas — “live” uzun emas, qisqa “i” bilan. Yana bir qurbon: “sheet” va “shit” — ha, siz ularni farqlamasangiz, inglizlar farqlaydi. “Sheet” — choyshab, “shit” — qo‘pol so‘z. Tabassum bilan uzun unlini cho‘zing.
scenes.say: A very common mistake: “live” versus “leave.” “I leave in Tashkent” is not acceptable — “live” takes the short “i.” One more victim: “sheet” versus “shit.” If you can't hear the difference, English speakers absolutely can — “sheet” is linen on a bed, and the other word is rude. Smile and stretch the long vowels.
scenes.say_uz: Juda keng tarqalgan xato: “live” va “leave”ni adashtirish. “I leave in Tashkent” qabul qilinmaydi — “live” qisqa “i” bilan. Yana bir qurbon: “sheet” va “shit”. Agar farqni eshitmasangiz, inglizlar eshitadi — “sheet” — choyshab, ikkinchisi qo‘pol so‘z. Tabassum qiling va uzun unlini cho‘zing.

scenes.title: Yakuniy vazifa: 20 ta minimal juftlik
board: th (5) · w/v (5) · short/long vowels (5) · schwa words (5)
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy vazifa: foningizga yigirma ta minimal juftlikni ovoz chiqarib yozib oling: besh th juftligi — think/sink, three/free, this/dis, bath/bathe, thigh/thy; besh w/v — wet/vet, wine/vine, west/vest, worse/verse, wine/fine emas (f demang); besh unli — ship/sheep, live/leave, cat/cut, bad/bed, fit/feet. Qolganlari: schwa so‘zlari — a cup of tea, about, today, banana, again.
scenes.say: Final task: record yourself reading twenty minimal pairs — five “th” pairs like think/sink, three/free, this/dis, bath/bathe, thigh/thy; five w/v — wet/vet, wine/vine, west/vest, worse/verse; five vowel pairs — ship/sheep, live/leave, cat/cut, bad/bed, fit/feet; and five schwa words — a cup of tea, about, today, banana, again.
scenes.say_uz: Yakuniy vazifa: yigirma ta minimal juftlikni ovoz chiqarib yozib oling. Besh th juftligi — think/sink, three/free, this/dis, bath/bathe, thigh/thy; besh w/v — wet/vet, wine/vine, west/vest, worse/verse; besh unli — ship/sheep, live/leave, cat/cut, bad/bed, fit/feet; beshta schwa so‘zi — a cup of tea, about, today, banana, again.

scenes.title: Bugun nimani o‘rgandik
board: Word stress · Sentence rhythm · Intonation · Linking
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Th tovushining ikki turini, w va v ni, qisqa a, bet, cut va i–ii farqini, schwa tovushini, so‘z urg‘usi harakatlanishini, jumla ritmini, savollar va sanash ohangini hamda bog‘lash va zaif shakllarni o‘rgandik. Keyingi darsda eng ko‘p uchraydigan o‘ttizta xato — grammar emas, nutq xatolarini ko‘rib chiqamiz.
scenes.say: Recap: the two “th” sounds, w versus v, the short vowels, short versus long “i,” schwa, moving word stress, sentence rhythm, question and list intonation, and linking with weak forms. Next time: the thirty most common mistakes.
scenes.say_uz: Xulosa: ikki th tovushi, w/v, qisqa unlilar, qisqa va uzun “i”, schwa, harakatlanadigan so‘z urg‘usi, jumla ritmi, savol va sanash ohangi, bog‘lash va zaif shakllar. Keyingi darsda eng ko‘p uchraydigan o‘ttizta xato.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi va keyingi dars
board: Homework: record 20 minimal pairs and a short text
Check: every “th” crisp · beat stays even
Next lesson: P1-21 the 30 most common mistakes
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: yigirma ta minimal juftlik va qisqa matnni — masalan, ob-havo yoki kundalik ishlaringiz haqida — telefoningizga yozib oling. Mezon: har bir “th” tiniq eshitilsin, har bir “w” lab bilan, jumla ritmi tekis ursin, savol ohanglari to‘g‘ri bo‘lsin. Keyingi darsda eng ko‘p uchraydigan o‘ttizta xato.
scenes.say: Homework: record twenty minimal pairs and one short text — the weather or your day. Success criteria: every “th” is crisp, every “w” comes from rounded lips, the rhythm stays even, and question tunes are right. Next time: the thirty most common mistakes.
scenes.say_uz: Uy vazifasi: yigirma ta minimal juftlik va qisqa matnni — ob-havo yoki kuningiz haqida — telefoningizga yozib oling. Mezon: har bir “th” tiniq, har bir “w” dumaloq lablar bilan, ritmiz tekis, savol ohanglari to‘g‘ri. Keyingi darsda eng ko‘p uchraydigan o‘ttizta xato.

homework_uz: Uy vazifasi: yigirma ta minimal juftlik va qisqa matnni — masalan, ob-havo yoki kuningiz haqida — telefoningizga yozib oling. Mezon: har bir “th” tiniq eshitilsin, har bir “w” dumaloq lablar bilan, jumla ritmi tekis ursin, savol ohanglari to‘g‘ri bo‘lsin. Keyingi darsda eng ko‘p uchraydigan o‘ttizta xato.
